prTitle: Add Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base VectorStore

content.motivation: This change adds support for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases as a vector store in Spring AI, enabling RAG applications to query managed knowledge bases without manually managing embeddings. It includes auto-configuration, starter modules, documentation, and a robust implementation with metadata filtering.
goodPoints: Well-implemented pagination logic using AWS SDK's nextToken to efficiently retrieve large result sets.
Comprehensive and well-structured unit and integration tests covering core functionality, filtering, and exception scenarios.
Correct use of Spring Boot auto-configuration annotations (@ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean) to ensure clean integration.
Logical separation of concerns between the store implementation and the filter expression converter.
Good use of builder pattern and Assert library for robust object construction and validation.
badPoints: The integration tests rely on environment variables, but there is no validation or descriptive error message provided if these variables are missing, potentially leading to silent test skipping.

The BedrockKnowledgeBaseVectorStore manual configuration documentation does not explicitly mention the requirement for an AWS SDK client bean definition, which could confuse users who prefer manual configuration.
content.suggestion: Add an initialization check or a custom @Configuration that provides a clear error message if the required environment variables are absent during development. Update the documentation to include a note about verifying that the BedrockAgentRuntimeClient is properly configured before use.

details: Uses a do-while loop to handle pagination via Bedrock's nextToken, ensuring efficient memory usage.
Implements a read-only store; add() and delete() operations explicitly throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Maps internal Knowledge Base metadata and document location types (S3, Confluence, SharePoint, etc.) to Spring AI document metadata format.
Recursively converts Spring AI filter expressions into native Bedrock RetrievalFilter structures.
Supports complex logical grouping (AND, OR, NOT) and all required comparison/list operators.
Activates based on class presence and the existence of the 'knowledge-base-id' property.
Provides a default BedrockAgentRuntimeClient bean using the AWS default credential chain if none is provided.

issues.title: Missing validation for required configuration properties
issues.detail: While the auto-configuration uses @ConditionalOnProperty, there is no validation to ensure that the provided 'knowledge-base-id' property is a valid format or that the AWS credentials are reachable before attempting to initialize the client.

interpretation.changeDescription: Introduced a new implementation of the VectorStore interface for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. This includes a new library (spring-ai-bedrock-knowledgebase-store), a corresponding Spring Boot auto-configuration module (spring-ai-autoconfigure-vector-store-bedrock-knowledgebase), and a starter dependency (spring-ai-starter-vector-store-bedrock-knowledgebase). The implementation allows performing similarity searches against an existing AWS Bedrock Knowledge Base and includes support for metadata filtering, reranking, and hybrid search configurations.
interpretation.changeMotivation: To provide native integration with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, enabling users to perform Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) operations leveraging Bedrock's fully managed service. This solution offloads document ingestion, chunking, and embedding management to AWS, and provides a standardized VectorStore abstraction that users can integrate into their existing Spring AI applications.

checklistItems.title: Does the filter expression converter adequately handle nested logical expressions and all supported data types, including nulls?

answer.finalAnswer: Yes, the filter expression converter adequately handles nested logical expressions and all supported data types, including nulls.
answer.analysis: The filter expression converter is explicitly designed to handle nested logical expressions (AND, OR, NOT) and all supported data types including nulls. The code shows recursive conversion of nested expressions and proper handling of null values via Document.fromNull().

evidence.reason: The filter expression converter is implemented to handle nested logical expressions using AND, OR, NOT operators, and supports comparison operators (EQ, NE, GT, GTE, LT, LTE), list operators (IN, NIN), and value types (String, Number, Boolean, Null). It also handles null values and converts them to Document.fromNull().
The converter uses a switch on ExpressionType and recursively processes nested expressions via convertAnd, convertOr, convertNot, which supports arbitrary nesting.
The converter extracts values from operands and handles nulls by returning Document.fromNull(), supporting nulls as valid values.

checklistItems.title: Is the pagination logic in the similarity search correctly implemented to handle large result sets without exhausting memory or exceeding API limits?

answer.finalAnswer: The pagination logic is correctly implemented to handle large result sets without exhausting memory or exceeding API limits by using a do-while loop with nextToken to fetch results in batches.
answer.analysis: The pagination logic is present in the BedrockKnowledgeBaseVectorStore.similaritySearch method (lines 100-140). It uses a do-while loop with nextToken to handle large result sets by making multiple API calls and collecting results in batches. The loop stops when topK results are reached or no more results are available. This prevents memory exhaustion by not loading all results at once and avoids exceeding API limits by using pagination tokens.

evidence.reason: The pagination logic is implemented in the similaritySearch method where it uses a do-while loop to paginate through retrieval results using nextToken until topK results are collected or no more results are available.
